AWPTCM-T47871.objective:
• A linkmon probe can be configured with type (icmp-ping), IP version, destination, interval, sample-size and enabled without error.
  • A trigger of type "linkmon probe" can be created and bound to probe state conditions (any, bad, good, unreachable).
  • A linkmon profile defines metric thresholds (e.g. latency bad-above value or consecutive lost probes); when the threshold is crossed the associated trigger activates.
  • When a probe enters the bad or unreachable state the corresponding trigger activates and a log entry records the event.
  • When a probe returns to the good state the good-condition trigger activates and a log entry records the event.
  • show linkmon probe (and probe-history) display valid configuration and collected data.

steps.description: Note: Related ART Tests linked in Traceability.
Configure a linkmon probe (type icmp-ping, destination, interval, sample-size, enable). Verify configuration is accepted and show linkmon probe displays the probe correctly.
Create a trigger of type linkmon probe and bind it to one of the probe conditions (bad, good, unreachable). Verify the trigger is created without error.
Apply a linkmon profile with a latency threshold (bad-above) or consecutive-lost-probes metric. Cause the probe to violate the threshold and confirm the matching trigger activates with a log entry.
Restore the probe to a passing state and confirm the good-condition trigger activates with the expected log entry.
Verify show linkmon probe-history (or equivalent) displays collected historic data after probe runs.
